headline: Largest Electric Aircraft Completes Maiden Flight, Fuels Regional Aviation Shift
deck: The successful test of a battery-powered demonstrator signals a future of lower emissions and operating costs for air travel.
body: The largest battery-electric aircraft completed its first test flight lasting nearly half an hour on August 12 at Plattsburgh International Airport in upstate New York. This landmark event, using just $5 of electricity, marks a significant step towards more sustainable regional aviation.

Comparable in size to a small regional airliner, the X1 aircraft achieved a maximum takeoff weight exceeding 25,000 pounds. Its battery-electric propulsion system delivered more than one megawatt of power during the maiden flight.

Current battery-electric systems typically sustain short flights, limited to about 100 to 200 miles. Heart Aerospace plans to address this range challenge with its 30-seat hybrid-electric regional airliner, the ES-30.

The ES-30 will integrate two inboard electric motors with commercial turboprop engines that run on jet fuel. This hybrid design enables 125 miles of all-electric flight and a 500-mile range when operating in hybrid mode.
United Airlines has already committed to eventually purchasing 100 aircraft from Heart Aerospace.

"Electric commercial aircraft have real potential to deliver a better travel experience for passengers while strengthening our business, and we look forward to Heart’s continued development of the ES-30 and its potential future role in United’s network," stated Michael Leskinen, chief financial officer of United Airlines.
Heart Aerospace anticipates beginning flight testing for the ES-30 in 2028. The company aims for commercial service certification by 2031.
The aviation industry faces high jet fuel prices, exacerbated by the US war with Iran. This economic pressure makes electric and hybrid aircraft an increasingly attractive alternative.

The successful X1 flight and the ES-30's development underscore a pivot in regional aviation's future. These advancements offer a viable path to significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions and operating costs, shaping more efficient and sustainable air travel.
